reviews.evidence: The core defines admissibility by finite-dimensional smooth fixed-vector spaces for compact open subgroups; the p-adic group, smooth representation, and local field prerequisites supply the stated setting and action.

The criterion identifies amenability with weak containment of the trivial representation in the left regular representation; locally compact group, regular representation, and weak containment are used directly.
The core is an invariant-mean definition on bounded functions over a locally compact group; the mean and group prerequisites are direct, while Haar measure is used for the Reiter equivalence later.

The theorem quantifies over a plurisubharmonic function and constructs an entire function with growth and L2 bounds; plurisubharmonic and entire-function concepts are direct prerequisites, and the latter was restored in this review.
The net is defined by convolution in L1(G), with shrinking-neighborhood support and norm one; locally compact groups and the L1 convolution algebra are the direct ambient concepts.

The center is defined through endomorphisms of every smooth representation and its action on irreducibles; reductive group, smooth representation, irreducibility, and Schur's lemma are used in the core and immediate characterization.

The statement decomposes smooth representations by inertial supercuspidal data and Levi subgroups; the reductive p-adic setting, smooth representations, characters, and supercuspidals are direct ingredients.

The construction uses Poisson extension, a linewise X-ray transform, and prescribed radial growth; those named analytic operators and the radial-growth condition are direct, while later estimates are consequences.

The theorem constructs a nonzero entire multiplier from bounded Fourier support and Lipschitz data; entire functions, Fourier support, Paley-Wiener control, and Lipschitz continuity are used in the statement.

Bochner's core represents a continuous positive-definite function by a unique finite positive regular Borel measure; Borel measure is the correct direct measure prerequisite, whereas probability is needed only for the normalized special case later.

The definition applies to an L2 equivalence class and uses its Fourier transform and essential support; almost-everywhere equality, Lp/L2 space, and bounded sets are direct, so the Lp prerequisite was added.

A coefficient is the scalar function g↦〈π(g)ξ,η〉 of a strongly continuous unitary representation on a Hilbert space; each listed representation, Hilbert, and inner-product concept is used immediately.
The core defines conjugate and contragredient actions from a unitary representation and Hilbert inner product; strong continuity, unitarity, Hilbert space, and inner product are direct ingredients.

The formula requires a locally compact group, left Haar measure, modular function, and L1 functions; the prerequisites provide exactly the measure and modular correction, while the companion algebra page is downstream and would create a cycle.

The convolution formula integrates products over a locally compact group against Haar measure and is stated almost everywhere; group, Haar measure, and a.e. notions are direct, with algebraic properties deferred.

The theorem assumes a porous set and a damping function, then derives an uncertainty estimate; porosity and damping function are direct hypotheses, while Fourier localization is encapsulated by the damping-function definition.

The definition requires bounded Fourier support, an L2 function, local L2 mass, and two decay bounds; bounded support and quantitative unique continuation capture the reusable conditions governing the construction.

The core assembles a measurable field of Hilbert spaces over a measure space into a direct-integral representation; measurability, Hilbert fields, strong continuity, and a.e. identification are all used directly.

The map sends boundary data through the Poisson extension to its normal derivative and identifies the fractional Laplacian/Hilbert-transform form; Poisson extension and Hilbert transform are the direct named operators.

The distinction is defined for a unitary representation of a locally compact group on a Hilbert space via invariant spectral subspaces; strong continuity, local compactness, and Hilbert structure are direct.
A distribution on a local field is a continuous linear functional on the test-function space; local-field topology and test functions are therefore direct, with representation-theoretic uses later.

The theorem selects the Haar measure on the Pontryagin dual that makes Fourier transformation unitary; locally compact abelian groups, duality, Haar measure, Fourier transform, and unitarity are all used in the core.

The proposition combines an exact plurisubharmonic weight with Poisson/X-ray control to obtain a multiplier; plurisubharmonic functions and the displayed analytic constructions are direct hypotheses, while estimates remain later.

The kernel description defines Fell neighborhoods through irreducible representations and their coefficient behavior; full group C-star algebra, irreducibles, unitary dual, and Fell topology are the concepts named in the statement.
Fell topology is defined by coefficient neighborhoods on the unitary dual and weak containment; locally compact groups, unitary representations, coefficients, and weak containment are direct.
The condition compares Haar measure of symmetric differences of compact measurable sets under translations; local compactness and Haar measure are direct, and the amenability equivalence is later.

The Fourier algebra consists of coefficient functions of the left regular representation; locally compact groups, regular representation, and coefficient functions are precisely the defining ingredients.

The theorem states Fourier transform converts L1 convolution on an LCA group into pointwise multiplication on the dual; abelian/local compact structure, Haar measure, convolution, transform, and duality are direct.

Inversion assumes both f and its transform are L1 and identifies a continuous representative almost everywhere; the L1-function prerequisite is direct and was added, alongside Haar/dual/transform and a.e. concepts.

The algebra is formed from matrix coefficients of strongly continuous unitary representations of a locally compact group; coefficient functions, representations, Hilbert spaces, and linear structure are used directly.
The transform integrates an L1 function against characters on an LCA group; local compactness, abelian duality, Haar measure, and L1 functions are the complete direct boundary.

The principle bounds simultaneous spatial and Fourier concentration for porous sets; porosity, Fourier localization, and the L2 norm are the operative concepts, with stronger variants referenced later.
The construction turns a positive-definite function into a cyclic unitary representation on a Hilbert space; positivity, Hilbert spaces, strong continuity, and cyclic vectors are direct.

The nonabelian transform is the integrated operator-valued representation against Haar measure and is measured using operator norm; the group, Haar, unitary dual, integrated form, and norm are direct.
The Haar integral is the positive left-translation-invariant functional/measure on a locally compact group; positive linear functionals, Haar measure, and local compactness supply the definition.
A Haar measure is a nonzero regular Borel measure invariant under left translation on a locally compact group; local compact group, Borel measure, and compact sets are direct.

The character is a distribution obtained from an admissible representation of a reductive p-adic group and tested against compactly supported functions; all those representation, field, test-function, distribution, and Haar concepts are used.

The algebra consists of Harish-Chandra Schwartz functions under convolution and involution, controlled by Xi on a real reductive group; group, Schwartz space, convolution, involution, and Xi are direct.

The space is defined by differential seminorms and Xi-weighted decay using the Lie algebra, maximal compact subgroup, and Cartan/Iwasawa data; these listed structural prerequisites are directly invoked.

Xi is a normalized spherical matrix coefficient and its integral formula uses the Iwasawa projection, restricted roots, and normalized Haar measure on K; representation, coefficient, Lie-group, and probability-measure prerequisites support those definitions.
